By allowing an admin level one button kick for group created public instances, Those public worlds with moderation, The moderators for public instances are being kicked from those group generated public worlds. 

This has had the knock on effect that groups such "Gangcrasher" are creating group public instances and removing moderators from them. Then ripping/stealing Avatars, committing sexual assault and general assault on people coming into the public instances.

This "groups" ban button also bans world creators from their own worlds.. 

This will also allow for Pehophile "groups" to create public group instances, remove moderation and allow them to remove anyone over the age of 16 and wait till the 7 year old kids show up in their public instance.. to diddle them.

This ... was a bad idea. and one that Tupper knew "would happen"  and sure enough .. IS happening right now to the Furhub.  I would suggest either A) public instance moderation team members be exempt from removal pf group public instances , or B) remove the button. or C) move it over that you have to be part of the group to join..

@{62def74b116f8244ab83190a|full_name}: I'm not saying that it isn't possible for these types of experiances to occur, Tau, but I will say that this is very extraneous from the experiance I've had of this instance type, and seems to border on hypothetical straw clutching and hyperbole to justify an end. If you have recordings showing that these scenarios are presently a problem, please share it so we can understand better.

But that aside, the fact is Avatar Ripping goes on in instances of all types most often covertly and completely undetected until after the fact - Group Public instances doesn't change this. And I don't believe World Creator moderation has served VRChat well over the years, which is why public instances are so renowned to be a wild west.

Regarding option A: If a Group is running an instance, and it is advertised as that Group's instance, then yes they should be able to remove even the World Creator because not being able to do so would elevate the creator above that Group's rules, and the instance is clearly associated to the group so it's their reputation on the line when it comes to moderation.

Regarding option B: Removal of the kick functionality would signficantly hinder valid uses cases for Groups Public worlds. Want to run a Public VR Portal for a furry con and easily share moderation access with a bunch of staff? Welp, now you can't, just gotta go back to sharing an account via Parsec. Want to run a public club event and modera- Oh that's out too.

Regarding option C: Again this doesn't acknowledge the valid use cases for why this instance type exists.

What I'd propose is treating this as a problem of user education by implementing a user modal that educates users when they attempt to join a Groups Public instance. Something like, "You're about to join a Groups Public instance. Groups Public instances may have different rules and different standards of moderation to Public instances" 

Cancel / View Group / OK

Add a tick box to the UI section to disable the modal for users who know what they're doing. This way users know that Groups Public can be a different experiance from Public, and are exercising informed choice when they join the instance.

Yes, Group Moderators shouldn't be able to kick the Group Owner.

But, they should be able to kick the World Creator because not being able to do so would elevate the World Creator above the rules and structure of the group that started the instance. (It's entirely possible for a World Creator to break a group's rules.)

@{618fa6ccbfca2a69d13f829c|full_name}: The problem here is twofold. By being able to remove world owner/creator moderation from PUBLIC instances you have completely missed the point as to the fallout as this situation will spiral out of control. 

World creators do not want public instances of their work to become the "black cat" And this will be exactly the model of several groups that like to kick in the teeth of the furry and LGBTQ+ community whenever they can. 

I, as the moderator of the FurHub  have had to commit to the VRC moderation team hundreds .. yes hundreds of reports on people  ranging from sexual assault to outright EAC bypass and crashing every month... every.. month.. 

Problem is this, this is not about the FurHub as much as it about the creators that advertise and sell their wares within it. We must be allowed to protect their interests as the very livelihoods of these creators do not want un-moderated instances with the KKK and Nazis running about screaming "DEATH TO THE FA**OTS" 

So, what can be done?  Well looks like we have no way to _opt out_ of the groups system.  So now we have to put a giant sign in the lobby. " if you are not in the moderated public instance you are as protected as the "black cat."  good luck 

If we are going to have a commerce system for asset creators, the public instances must not only be moderated, But moderated in ways that are effective . 

As for what we have dealt with in some of these gangmonkey "groups" that come into FurHub moderation team has about 20 terabytes of video we can show you.

From your post you have no idea what is going to be wrought upon players in these public group instances. And our ability to stop and report them is going to become impossible.

@{62def74b116f8244ab83190a|full_name}: I don't think this is as big an issue as you make it out to be but I respect your perspective. The only reason I'm doubtful is because the vast majority of VRChat public instances are completely unmoderated and you seem to be commenting from the position of an edge case that is not representative of how things work in a broader context. The edge case being that of a world that somehow has, miraculously, moderation in all public instances, at all hours of the day and is a utopia for all. (Obviously I'm being sarcastic; No public instance is that good, not even FurHub - I cannot recall a time that I haven't needed to rely upon Vote Kick to remove trolls while I've been there, but Vote Kick is still very effective.)

If one accepts that the vast majority of world creators have neither the time nor the resources to effectively organise delegated moderation of their public instances, then I struggle to see how one can assert Groups Public, on the whole, worsens the overall VRChat experiance.

Groups Public is not perfect, but I think with some tweaks, it could be improved:

* User education modal upon attempting to enter the instance.

* Only list Groups Public instances if someone with Moderation permissions has entered the instance in the last hour or so. (Allows event moderators to move between multiple instances, but ensures they get delisted when no longer in use.)

* Allow Groups to convert a Groups Public to a Public when they're done with it.

* Order Groups Public to the bottom of the instance list to better reflect their ad-hoc nature.

These are common sense improvements that still preserve the core of what was a much requested feature by the VRChat social event community.

@{618fa6ccbfca2a69d13f829c|full_name}: So I think you really have no idea what United Moderation , a group that spans several worlds that supports the LGBTQ+ and Furry communities .. You have no idea what we deal with on a daily basis. 

We have a database and systems for recording and reporting  what goes on , and for the most part we have staff on call when there is an issues. Much like Furry Hideout has ( with their own system ) 

Yes, there is live moderation in the Furhub and several other worlds and we have managed to curate public places that are fairly safe and free of the worst of it.  

If you knew how bad it really is, You would realize how bad this is for any space looking to serve creators. And how this .. thing  where not only We the mods try and protect. But that the world creators, the ones who actually make the worlds can be kicked. 

This thing alone has groups believing that they OWN the world they are in. They do not, but try and tell them that and they kick you out.

@{62def74b116f8244ab83190a|full_name}: You would be mistaken in your assumptions; Having been involved in moderation for various notable VRChat events and communities I'm well familiar with the systems, processes and avenues of information exchange that frequently exist, as well as the types of issues that arise. (Though granted things for FurHub may be worse as it does seem to attract more than its fair share of trouble)

But it is actually from those experiances that I have first party experiance as a moderator to say that we needed and now have Groups Public instances for the good health of the VRChat social and events community - Which is why VRChat have implemented this much requested feature.

However, that being said, I'm entirely open to discussion around tweaking the implementation to be less disruptive to existing moderation structures, whilst still allowing Groups Public instances to exist, moderate how they wish and remove who they wish. Refer to the previous dot points for what I have in mind.

@{618fa6ccbfca2a69d13f829c|full_name}: Really there is few solutions and in talking to several moderated world owners the one they like the most is "opting out" of the groups. As it stands with the system set to be able to Ban world creators, Not instance creator, but the people who spent months creating their worlds are VERY unhappy that they can be kicked from their own creations. 

We have a couple that have considered pulling their worlds entirely if this remains the case. What it says to them and myself included is we do not have rights to our own public instanced worlds. We could give two figs about private. But if there is a public instance of our worlds we should not be able to be kicked from them. 

I have been told by groups who "Instanced" our worlds that not only do they own them, But we gave up our rights to ownership to VRC the moment we uploaded them.. So far VRC will not confirm OR deny that indeed, we are no longer the owner of our worlds once they are uploaded.  

So now we are in the realm, of "what are IP creators rights" arguments because We are being shouted at by these "Group created" instances that we not only have no rights to demand not to be evicted from our creations, But we are not to evict their friends (even if they are known crasher and EAC bypass permaban) 

So.. I think before we even begin to discuss what should be done, I think every world creator needs to know 

What are our rights as content creators under VRC.

@{62def74b116f8244ab83190a|full_name}: Alright. We seem to be conflating "The way things are" with being a "right", so please forgive me for what will be a lengthy explanation for those reading.

------  BEGIN IP DISCUSSION------

Intellectual property questions are readily answered by Sections 9.2 and 9.3 of the Terms of Service. Section 13 deals with the platform's right to change how the platform works at anytime. These sections are written in plain English and can be found at https://hello.vrchat.com/legal - What follows is my explanation of those sections.

World creators (by default) own their content as it exists outside of the VRChat platform.

By electing to upload that world to VRChat, Content Creators have given VRChat an irrevocable license to do a long list of things, including use, distribute, modify, monetise and sub-license the content to anyone at its sole discretion, worldwide. (Even if you later delete the content, they can still use it how they wish and grant others the right to do the same.)

Seperately from this, the content creator has directly given any user of VRChat a license to access and use the content as permitted by the functionality of the platform. (Which can change at any time per Section 13.)

There is nothing in the Terms of Service that grants any specific rights to Content Creators in terms of features or powers within VRChat once content has been uploaded and this includes the right to manage Public instances or to dictate how it is used. Hence, technically both the parties you refer to are wrong: All world instances are legally owned by VRChat using the content of creators licensed under Section 9.2 of the Terms of Service, and as a product of the functionality VRChat has chosen to implement, it has permitted (Not as a right) World Creators to to have some limited permissions in Public instances, and Groups to have the same permissions in Groups Public instances, subject to Section 13. (IE: It can change that at any time, which again means it is not a right, but a custom.)

This is consistent with the operation of other social VR platforms, and I'd invite you to read the Terms of Service for any one of them to validate that fact. Personally, I'm not sure how there could be legitimate quesitons surrounding this given it has been written so plainly; I suspect the questions are disingenuous. 

------ END IP DISCUSSION ------ 

Seperate to the above, the idea of opting out of Groups has been floated in one other feedback thread but was later watered down on consensus as it would remove flexibility and increase the minefield that VRChat social/event communities need to navigate when selecting worlds to visit, hence its safe to say that this suggestion is not in the interests of the platform as a whole.

@{618fa6ccbfca2a69d13f829c|full_name}: Are you an representative of VRChat?

And very important, I cannot find the section the specifically states that VRC has the right to take content that you have deleted from their platform and use it as they wish.  

Section 9.1 says this  “User Content”). As between you and VRChat, you retain copyright and any other proprietary rights in the User Content you Post, subject to the licenses granted in this TOS or in any other agreement between you and VRChat.

That seems to fly in the face of that statement you made. 

Regulation of public worlds seems to be by fiat of VRC to allow us to use tools to ban or eject people violating the TOS seems to be outlined here. 

""9.6 Where permitted by functionality within the Platform, you may delete copies or instances of your User Content that you have uploaded to your Account through the normal functionality of the Platform. If you delete your User Content through use of that functionality, the licenses granted by you in this Section 9 to your User Content terminate as described in this Section 9.6 with respect to the particular copies or instances of your User Content that you have deleted.""

So as the creator, it looks here that we could, or should be able to delete instances. So if a group instance is running afoul of the TOS , we should be allowed to delete those instances? . 

I am good with that. 

So if we discover gangmonkey X  groups are making instances , we can delete those instances if they are violating the TOS .. which they are.. they always are ..

@{62def74b116f8244ab83190a|full_name}: No, I am not a representative of VRChat, as denoted by lack of a tag indicating such. However being an active participant in the VR social events community I do have a different perspective from yours. Hence, my participation here is defined by my desire to ensure the needs of those users are well-represented in any discussion pertaining to features they depend upon.

On the topic of Section 9.6, I stand corrected on the irrevocability of the license which was determined by reading of section 9.2 - Truthfully I didn't read that far but you are correct, deleting content from the platform does extinguish VRChat's license to use the content. (Though I'm sure you'd agree that is of minimal relevance to the discussion at hand, since it seems like you'd prefer to keep your world on the platform, but have the platform follow your rules instead of theirs.)

However on a latter point I believe you are mistaken. The term 'instance' as used in Section 9.6 does not refer to world instances in the way that you're intending it to but rather an copy or instance of an object in terms of the IP, which is only ever supplied once to VRChat. Though... debating the meaning of the word instance is irrelevant as Section 9.6 clearly starts with "Where permitted by functionality within the Platform"

Does the platform offer you the functionality to delete specific world instances? No. 

What does the platform allow you to do? The ability to remove FurHub from the platform entirely... in which case other worlds will simply be used instead. (Furry Hideout and FurLounge are quite popular afterall.)

With regard to the custom of Public instances having owners with moderation permissions, I'd hazard a guess that this was about ensuring that someone other than VRChat could be viewed as 'responsible' for the world instance, in line with Friends/Friends+/Invite/Invite+ instances having owners. If that is indeed the purpose, then Groups Public and Groups+ instances still meet the intention of this stance - There is a clearly designated group that owns the instance that can moderate it, with a clearly designated owner.

@{618fa6ccbfca2a69d13f829c|full_name}: Totally agreed.

Basically just remove the world creator's moderation powers, then there won't be these weird moderation arguments ever again. Not all world creators are saints, and instance owners should always be the highest authority. If world creators want to have moderation powers in a public instance they should make their own group public instance, or they should use private instances.

See: [remove-world-creator-moderation-powers](https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/remove-world-creator-moderation-powers)

If only group moderators have moderation powers, then it is an internal group issue if they begin kicking each other. Or once world creator moderation powers are removed, moderators can be changed to be immune to moderator kicks.

(PS: Why aren't kicks logged? [Canny post.](https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/group-audit-log-should-show-when-a-user-is-kicked-from-a-group-instance))

@{62def74b116f8244ab83190a|full_name}: To put it simply, @{618fa6ccbfca2a69d13f829c|full_name} is right.

The obvious way you are supposed to deal with "gangmonkey groups", "pedophile groups", hackers, crasher, and whatever else your *organization* deals with, is to report them to VRChat's trust and safety. You can report groups too, if they are doing something that breaks the terms of service.

As outlined in the legal pages, other users have the rights to use the uploaded content in any way the platform allows. Put simply, users are allowed to make Group Public instances and moderate them however they want. As @{618fa6ccbfca2a69d13f829c|full_name} said, the only issue with Group Public instances is that users of VRChat still aren't completely used to them still. Users need to be made more aware of what a Group Public instance is, and the rules of the owning group needs to be communicated better to the user when they join a Group Public instance.

If a world creator doesn't like that a certain group is making Group Public instances of their world, then there is nothing they can do about it. The world creator's best option is to start a normal Public instance and see if it can get more popularity than the undesired Group Public instances. Or the world creator can make their own Group Public instance with a group they control, they can then add a sign in their world that politely suggests that users use the world's *official* group's Group Public instances.

Alternatively, the world creator can just unpublish their world. That way there won't be any Public instances of either type.

@{610d538d5303a82960a415b4|full_name}: First are you a representative of VRChat? 

Second, please show me where that the creation of other instances negates the rights of the creator of the IP to control how it is used or abused. That as a creator of a world you have no right to protect it except to "pull it down" 

Ill wait ..

@{62def74b116f8244ab83190a|full_name}: Aside from the one thing about irrevocability of the license, everything that @{618fa6ccbfca2a69d13f829c|full_name} said is in the Terms of Service. I am sure you aren't a legal expect either and if that is your requirement for having a discussion then talk with you is indeed pointless.

But sure, I will throw this very quickly at you, and you can proceed to ignore it if you don't want to believe it.

"8.2. Limited License Grant to VRChat" gives VRChat permission to use the creation and share it with users. "8.3. Limited License Grant to Other Users" grants other users of VRChat permission to use the creation. In other words, by uploading content to VRChat, you are allowing VRChat to give other users permission to use the content in any way the platform supports.

There is nothing in the Terms of Service or in the Community Guidelines that says the world creator has complete control over who can use their world or how. The only rules that even remotely seem to mention such is the Creator Guidelines, here it mentions that world creators aren't allowed to pre-emptively punish or block users from using their worlds via Udon scripting if the users haven't done anything wrong in THAT instance.

As I understand it, the purpose of VRChat Groups is to give small communities the ability to make their own Group Public instances of any public world and moderate it however they want, as long as it abides by the Terms of Service and Community Guidelines. From my understanding of what your *organization* does, from reading what you wrote in this thread, it sounds like your *organization* should make a VRChat Group and use Group Public instances so you can moderate those. This allows for users to pick the instances they want, based on the level of moderation they are ok with. If a user wants your *organization*'s moderation, they can join your *organization*'s Group Public instances.

Basically, the world creator having moderation powers in all instances of their world is an old rule from before VRChat Groups were implemented. Now that VRChat Groups exists, the world creator doesn't need those moderation powers in all instances of their world. This is why I am voicing my opinion about how [world creator moderation powers should be removed](https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/remove-world-creator-moderation-powers).
This is desperately needed. The kick/ban system should work like Discord's.
